summary: Wired Datasette startup through the ASGI lifespan. In app.py, Datasette.__init__ sets _setup_db_done=False and _startup_lock=asyncio.Lock() (both normal and RuntimeError workaround branches). Added async _startup_sequence(), the single idempotent, lock-guarded entry point: returns if both _startup_invoked and _setup_db_done are set, otherwise under the lock it runs immutable-database table_counts precompute then invoke_startup(). Removed the local setup_db from Datasette.app() and rewired it to AsgiLifespan(on_startup=[_startup_sequence]) then AsgiRunOnFirstRequest(on_startup=[_startup_sequence]). In utils/asgi.py, AsgiLifespan now catches startup/shutdown exceptions and sends lifespan.startup.failed / lifespan.shutdown.failed instead of escaping; AsgiRunOnFirstRequest passes lifespan scopes through and uses a lock + re-check so concurrent first requests wait for startup. cli.py serve now calls _startup_sequence() instead of invoke_startup(). 157 passed, 4 skipped.
concerns: Verify the AsgiRunOnFirstRequest lifespan-scope pass-through does not double-run hooks if a server ever sends lifespan.startup for a request-scope path.
Confirm the --get CLI path (run_sync(ds.invoke_startup)) still works, since only the serve path was switched to _startup_sequence per the task spec.
